source_title: World Bank IFC AI travel survey
unit_or_scope: more than 2200 IFC-portfolio companies across 85 plus countries
direct_observation: About 40 percent reported some AI use; nearly a quarter used AI internally and externally; digital-first and younger firms adopted more and regional sector differences were large
closed_stage: adoption prevalence depth categories firm-age and digital divide
missing_stage: representative economy-wide adoption quality productivity jobs local suppliers and value retention
next_test: compare matched local multinational small analogue and digital firms on depth and outcomes

source_title: World Bank emerging-market adoption depth update
direct_observation: AI adoption can rise rapidly while sophisticated use remains slower and concentrated; skills and organizational capability support movement from experimentation to deeper integration
missing_stage: named capability build local adaptation worker outcomes and durable productivity
next_test: follow firms from experiment to adapted workflow/product and later performance

source_title: World Bank WDR 2026 adopt adapt advance
direct_observation: Countries can benefit without building frontier models but must adapt AI to local languages institutions data and needs while building skills infrastructure interoperability and small-AI access
missing_stage: inclusive jobs service quality sovereignty and supplier dependence
next_test: join local adaptation complements to user service and value retention

source_title: World Bank South Asia Economic Update 2026
unit_or_scope: South Asian firms and public-service/AI ecosystem
direct_observation: AI adoption rises but trails frontier; about 23 percent of Indian firms report use versus 43 percent in US and sophisticated-use gap is wider; small-firm support local innovation skills energy data and infrastructure are constraints
missing_stage: firm adaptation local ownership job quality public-service outcome energy affordability and data security
next_test: compare firm size region and use depth with service and labor outcomes

source_title: World Bank South Asia industrial-policy evidence
unit_or_scope: multinational affiliates GVC suppliers and local firms in South Asia
direct_observation: Multinational affiliates lead AI-skill adoption; higher pre-ChatGPT exposure is associated with larger post-release hiring reductions, especially among multinationals, with shifts toward complementary roles
missing_stage: local value learning supplier capability worker transition bargaining power and demand displacement
next_test: trace named affiliate/supplier/local firm through adoption hiring task and value-retention outcomes

source_title: World Bank Adopting Fast and Slow
direct_observation: Firm adoption nearly tripled while sophisticated use remained slower and concentrated; managers expected future productivity and employment gains
missing_stage: realized productivity employment local capability and independent outcome validation
next_test: match expected gains to firm accounts worker data and downstream customer outcomes
